title: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 23](/bible/exodus/23)

**[Exodus 23:1-2](/bible/exodus/23#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/23#v1)</sup> Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/23#v2)</sup> Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:

- Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut.
- Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 4:14-17](/bible/proverbs/4#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/proverbs/4#v14)</sup> Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/proverbs/4#v15)</sup> Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/proverbs/4#v16)</sup> For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/proverbs/4#v17)</sup> For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

    Enter not into the path of the wicked; they sleep not except they have done mischief, and they drink the wine of violence.
  - **[Proverbs 1:10-15](/bible/proverbs/1#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/proverbs/1#v10)</sup> My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/proverbs/1#v11)</sup> If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/proverbs/1#v12)</sup> Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit:
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/proverbs/1#v13)</sup> We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/proverbs/1#v14)</sup> Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/proverbs/1#v15)</sup> My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:

    If sinners entice thee, consent thou not; walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil.
  - **[Proverbs 19:2](/bible/proverbs/19#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/proverbs/19#v2)</sup> Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.

    That the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
  - **[Isaiah 59:6-7](/bible/isaiah/59#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/isaiah/59#v6)</sup> Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/isaiah/59#v7)</sup> Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths.

    The works of sinners are works of iniquity; their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood.

- Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a [Romans 16:17](/bible/romans/16#v17) marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 1:17](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v17)</sup> Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.

    Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's.
  - **[Romans 16:17](/bible/romans/16#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/romans/16#v17)</sup> Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

    Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine, and avoid them; once put out, that judgment is followed.

**[Exodus 23:3](/bible/exodus/23#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/23#v3)</sup> Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.

- Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great.
- In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 1:16-17](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v16)</sup> And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/1#v17)</sup> Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.

    Judge righteously between every man and his brother; ye shall not respect persons in judgment, but hear the small as well as the great.

**[Exodus 23:4-5](/bible/exodus/23#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/23#v4)</sup> If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/23#v5)</sup> If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.

- If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean.
- [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people.
- Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1)</sup> Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ox or his sheep go astray, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v2)</sup> And if thy brother be not nigh unto thee, or if thou know him not, then thou shalt bring it unto thine own house, and it shall be with thee until thy brother seek after it, and thou shalt restore it to him again.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v3)</sup> In like manner shalt thou do with his ass; and so shalt thou do with his raiment; and with all lost thing of thy brother’s, which he hath lost, and thou hast found, shalt thou do likewise: thou mayest not hide thyself.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v4)</sup> Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ass or his ox fall down by the way, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.

    Thou shalt not see thy brother's ox go astray and hide thyself; in any case bring it again to thy brother, even a brother thou knowest not, and help him lift his ass or his ox when it is fallen.
  - **[Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/19#v17)</sup> Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/19#v18)</sup> Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.

    Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear grudge against the children of thy people, but love thy neighbour as thyself.
  - **[Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44)**
    > <sup>[44](/bible/matthew/5#v44)</sup> But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

    Love your enemies: read with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4, the enemy to be loved and helped is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee.

**[Exodus 23:6-8](/bible/exodus/23#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/23#v6)</sup> Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/23#v7)</sup> Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/23#v8)</sup> And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.

- Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment.
- Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked.
- Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

**[Exodus 23:9](/bible/exodus/23#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/23#v9)</sup> Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger: for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

- Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

**[Exodus 23:10-11](/bible/exodus/23#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/23#v10)</sup> And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the fruits thereof:
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/23#v11)</sup> But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard.

- Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor.
- The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

**[Exodus 23:12](/bible/exodus/23#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/23#v12)</sup> Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed.

- Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath.
- When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

**[Exodus 23:13](/bible/exodus/23#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/23#v13)</sup> And in all things that I have said unto you be circumspect: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.

- Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name.
- The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them.
- Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

  Precepts:
  - **[Matthew 12:25-27](/bible/matthew/12#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/matthew/12#v25)</sup> And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/matthew/12#v26)</sup> And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/matthew/12#v27)</sup> And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.

    Christ said, If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? He mentioned the name of another god and did no sin.
  - **[Joshua 23:6-8](/bible/joshua/23#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/joshua/23#v6)</sup> Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left;
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/joshua/23#v7)</sup> That ye come not among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them:
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/joshua/23#v8)</sup> But cleave unto the Lord your God, as ye have done unto this day.

    Neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them, but cleave unto the Lord your God.
  - **[Deuteronomy 13:6-8](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v6)</sup> If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v7)</sup> Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/13#v8)</sup> Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:

    If thy nearest kin entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent unto him nor hearken unto him.

**[Exodus 23:14-17](/bible/exodus/23#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/23#v14)</sup> Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/23#v15)</sup> Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Abib; for in it thou camest out from Egypt: and none shall appear before me empty:)
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/23#v16)</sup> And the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou hast sown in the field: and the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/23#v17)</sup> Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord God.

- Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year.
- The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
- None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses.
- The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

  Precepts:
  - **[Luke 22:1](/bible/luke/22#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/luke/22#v1)</sup> Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.

    The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover; the two names are one feast.

**[Exodus 23:18-19](/bible/exodus/23#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/23#v18)</sup> Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/23#v19)</sup> The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother’s milk.

- Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God.
- Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

**[Exodus 23:20-22](/bible/exodus/23#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/exodus/23#v20)</sup> Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/23#v21)</sup> Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/exodus/23#v22)</sup> But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.

- Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ.
- If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

**[Exodus 23:23-31](/bible/exodus/23#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/exodus/23#v23)</sup> For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/exodus/23#v24)</sup> Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/exodus/23#v25)</sup> And ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/exodus/23#v26)</sup> There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I will fulfil.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/exodus/23#v27)</sup> I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/exodus/23#v28)</sup> And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/exodus/23#v29)</sup> I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/exodus/23#v30)</sup> By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/exodus/23#v31)</sup> And I will set thy bounds from the Red sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand; and thou shalt drive them out before thee.

- The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images.
- Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land.
- The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

**[Exodus 23:32-33](/bible/exodus/23#v32)**

> <sup>[32](/bible/exodus/23#v32)</sup> Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/exodus/23#v33)</sup> They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.

- Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.
